messages:
Sarah L.: Heads up — I pushed an exports map change to @redwood/sdk-js to DRY up CJS/ESM entries and it broke the edge sample in CI.
Sarah L.: New package.json snippet I added:
{
  "exports": {
    "./*": {"require": "./dist/cjs/*.js", "import": "./dist/esm/*.js"},
    "./node": {"require": "./dist/cjs/node.js", "default": "./dist/esm/node.js"}
  }
}
Sarah L.: Edge runtime (V8 isolate) fails to resolve "@redwood/sdk-js/edge" and CI shows a file URL resolution error.
Mike P.: Paste of CI error:
```
Error: Cannot find module 'file:///repo/node_modules/@redwood/sdk-js/dist/esm/edge.js'
While resolving import "@redwood/sdk-js/edge" from /workspace/samples/chat/edge/index.mjs
```
Ben K.: Sounds like the wildcard mapping and conditional fields confuse non-Node resolvers (bun/deno/edge embedder). They treat the "./*" differently and sometimes prefer the CJS path or don't map extless imports.
Jamie (eng): We're also seeing TypeScript server pick up the cjs declaration files for auto-imports — IDEs offering wrong signatures for edge imports.
Sarah L.: I didn't expect the wildcard to be that brittle. Reverting to explicit subpath entries for edge should be safer (./edge, ./edge.mjs, ./edge.js) and adding explicit conditionals for runtimes that use "default" vs "import".
Ben K.: Can we patch-release a revert? Also add CI that runs the edge sample bundler and a test that verifies declaration file paths resolve correctly.
Sarah L.: Opening revert PR now. Will also create an issue and add a canary publish for teams to smoke test. Apologies for the breakage :facepalm:. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/789 (revert + tests).
devex-bot: created issue #412: "exports map wildcard causes edge sample resolution failures" and assigned to Sarah L.
Mike P.: After revert let's publish a canary and sweep internal sample apps. Also add a small doc note about subpath stability so integrators know to avoid fragile wildcards.
Ben K.: +1. Thanks for catching and moving quickly.
Jamie (eng): Ping me if you want help running the smoke matrix across our internal runtimes.
